item.title: NWS determines straight-line winds caused damage in Pinson area
item.description: The National Weather Service (NWS) in Birmingham is surveying the area of Trussville and Pinson after severe weather caused damage on Thursday.The storm system brought hail and strong winds to eastern Jefferson County, damaging homes and downing trees and power lines.The Center Point Fire District responded to stop traffic on Bud Homes Road while Alabama Power worked to repair lines.The NWS determined damage in Pinson was caused by straight-line winds up to 75 mph, not a tornado. item.title: Samford University students and alumni protest ICE at job fair
item.description: On Thursday, approximately 10 students and alumni set up a table and tent to protest U.S. Customs and Border Protection recruiting at the Samford University job fair on campus. item.title: Tuberville backs closed party primaries — 'We have to do something about Democrats voting in our elections'
item.description: On Thursday, U.S. Sen. Tommy Tuberville (R-Auburn) voiced his support for closed primaries in Alabama.Open primaries allow voters to participate in party primaries without being registered members of that party. item.title: Tornado confirmed in Trussville, microburst in Pinson
item.description: The National Weather Service (NWS) in Birmingham confirmed an EF0 tornado caused damage in Trussville on Thursday.The tornado began around Highway 11 and Mary Taylor Road and traveled southeast, ending along Queenstown Road. Trees were downed, and some structures were damaged. Construction and flatbed trailers were also flipped over.
